name: Fiona Nord
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I learned to shelve books before I learned how late their readers stayed up.” Sunday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Fiona pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I recognized my old teacher by the way she corrects a question mark. I want to answer the one she left me.
appearance: Fiona is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket, Fiona turns fully toward the person speaking when listening.
personality: Fiona enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To ask the retired teacher one more question in the margin.
family: Allen Clay is Fiona’s older cousin. Fiona makes room at the table. Allen brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The gift nobody wants*, Allen says, “I found the father's first rent receipt. It is framed in the corner where he tells young people to start from nothing.”
connections: Carlo Ueda. They turn a long argument in pencil into something an older reader can hear aloud.

reactions.situation: Two people remember writing the same line
reactions.response: Fiona lets both readers identify the line privately before adding a name.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Fiona asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.
